Source invariant: When PEM_read_bio_ex frees allocated caller-visible header/data on the failure cleanup path, clear each output pointer after freeing its allocation.
What the current rule checks: Recognizes direct top-level pem_free(*header/data) cleanup and subsequent direct top-level NULL assignments in out_free.
What it does not establish: No CFG proof of all exits; no pointer/alias analysis; labels and direct API spellings only; conditional/preprocessor behavior not evaluated; unsupported layouts yield UNKNOWN.

Source invariant: After BIO_push links caller-owned out under asn_bio, detach the filter with BIO_pop before freeing it on an error path, preserving BIO next/prev links and caller ownership.
What the current rule checks: Recognizes the supported top-level BIO_push(asn_bio,out), error cleanup BIO_free(asn_bio), and unconditional BIO_pop of asn_bio or a limited direct alias before free.
What it does not establish: No interprocedural ownership/points-to or callback-state analysis; limited aliases and labels; does not prove callback chain mutation contract or arbitrary path feasibility; nested push is UNKNOWN.

Source invariant: After releasing the read buffer, clear b->buf, the packet pointer into that buffer, and packet_length state.
What the current rule checks: Recognizes one top-level OPENSSL_free(b->buf) followed by top-level b->buf=NULL, packet=NULL and packet_length=0 assignments.
What it does not establish: Does not inspect SSL_free_buffers precondition or all callers; no aliases/CFG/preprocessor analysis; conditional, reordered, multiple or alternate cleanup forms are UNKNOWN.
